title: Keep attachment downloads inside the attachment store

blocks.text: Ticket attachments are downloaded with `GET /attachments?name=T-118/screenshot.txt`, and the name is used to find the file under the store's directory. Next to that directory, on the same disk, are the service's configuration, an export area, and an older store. Someone has also put a link inside the store that leads to the export area. On some hosts the store's directory is configured through a link of its own.

Write `locate(name)` in `src/main/java/practice/AttachmentStore.java`. A name that leads to one of the store's files returns that file, however the name is spelled. A name that would lead to any other file is refused with a `SecurityException`. The store must keep working on the hosts that configure it through a link.
About four lines in total. The tests build the directories and links in a temporary directory.

cases.says: names of the store's own files, including one with a .. that stays inside, are read
a name whose .. elements climb above the store is refused
a sibling directory whose name begins with the store's name is outside the store
a symbolic link inside the store that points outside it does not give access to the files it points at
when the store's directory is configured through a link, its own files are still served

origin.section: A Symlink Inside the Base Points Anywhere; Check the Real Path

concepts: A requested path stays inside its base only if the resolved path is normalized and then compared with Path.startsWith; without normalize() .. escapes, and a string prefix accepts a sibling directory whose name begins like the base.
normalize() never reads the disk, so a symbolic link inside the base can lead outside it; toRealPath() follows links, and the base must be compared as a real path too.
